chunks.label: How verbs work
chunks.rationale: The machinery every form below uses: which group a verb is in, how its stem shifts, the te/ta sound changes, and the few exceptions.
chunks.interference: Godan lookalikes like kaeru and hairu get treated as ichidan (kaeta, haita instead of kaetta, haitta).

chunks.label: Now and not
chunks.rationale: Present and negative in both registers: the four forms behind most sentences.
chunks.interference: Plain and polite pairs blur together; aranai for nai, and -u verbs losing their w (kaanai for kawanai).

chunks.label: The past
chunks.rationale: The same four slots moved into the past, plain and polite.
chunks.interference: -nakatta used for 'not yet' where mada -tenai belongs; dropped sound changes (kaeta for kaetta).

chunks.label: The te-form
chunks.rationale: The te-form and the requests built on it: do it, please do it, please don't.
chunks.interference: -naide (please don't) confused with -nakute; bare -te heard as unfinished rather than as a request.

chunks.label: Ongoing and done
chunks.rationale: te-form plus iru: what's going on, what was going on, and what hasn't happened yet.
chunks.interference: -teru as a resulting state (kekkon shiteru, kiteru) heard as an action in progress; shittenai for shiranai.

chunks.label: Wanting and inviting
chunks.rationale: Wants, suggestions and invitations, from casual to polite.
chunks.interference: -mashou (assumes yes) vs -masen ka (leaves room to refuse); kaerou (let's go home) vs kaeru.

chunks.label: If and when
chunks.rationale: The four conditionals; -tara covers most needs and the others add shades.
chunks.interference: All four translate as 'if': -to can't be followed by a request, nara looks ahead, -tara means once it's happened.

chunks.label: Must and don't have to
chunks.rationale: Obligation, permission and prohibition, mostly built from -nai and -te.
chunks.interference: -nakya (have to) vs -nakute mo ii (don't have to); -cha dame (mustn't) vs -chau (did it).
